chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father who said: He narrated to me a sheikh from among our companions from the Kufans.

He said: Isa ibn Shaqaf entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he was a magician who would come to him, and he would take payment for that. So he said to him: I am your ransom, I am a man whose profession was magic, and I would take payment for it, and it was my livelihood. And I had performed Hajj, and God graced me with meeting you, and I have repented to God, the Mighty and Majestic. Is there for me any way out of anything of it? He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Release (the knots) and do not tie (new ones).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a magician who repents but continues his trade?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Isa ibn Shaqaf, a professional magician, seeks clarification from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the sufficiency of his repentance to exit the profession of magic. The Imam’s concise advice, 'release and do not tie' (ḥull wa lā taʿqid), is interpreted by Shia scholars as a directive to completely sever the contractual and practical ties to the craft, ensuring a definitive break from the earnings derived from it rather than merely continuing the practice. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the purity of income (mal ṭayyib) and the necessity of abandoning the specific cause of impurity when repenting from a specialized trade.
